s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction with highly vascularized mass
salient_findings: Voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
Hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
key_facts: Woman in her 30s with no relevant medical history
Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction
Endoscopic examination found a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra
MRI confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Radioiodine scintigraphy found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions
Sinonasal tumor had low uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy
Serum thyroglobulin level was significantly elevated at 4432 ng/mL
Biopsy results confirmed metastasis

shortlist.label: Metastatic Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum thyroglobulin and biopsy results confirm metastasis

shortlist.label: Metastatic Follicular Thyroid Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Highly vascularized mass and metastasis to bone

shortlist.label: Metastatic Poorly Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive tumor behavior and distant metastases

shortlist.label: Juvenile Nasopharyngeal Angiofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Highly vascularized mass in the nasal cavity

shortlist.label: Nasal Cavity Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Voluminous and pulsatile mass in the nasal cavity

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a highly vascularized mass in the nasal cavities, along with the findings of hypervascular tumors in the nasal cavity, thyroid, rib, and vertebra on imaging studies, and significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin levels, points towards a metastatic thyroid carcinoma. The low uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy for the sinonasal tumor but considerable uptake for the rib and vertebral lesions suggests a metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma, which can have variable iodine uptake.

rejected.label: Metastatic Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma
rejected.why: Papillary thyroid carcinoma typically has a different metastatic pattern and often retains radioiodine uptake.

rejected.label: Metastatic Poorly Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma
rejected.why: Poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma is less common and typically presents with more aggressive features and less differentiated cells on biopsy, which is not highlighted in the case.

rejected.label: Juvenile Nasopharyngeal Angiofibroma
rejected.why: This condition is more common in adolescent males and does not typically present with systemic metastases or significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin levels.

rejected.label: Nasal Cavity Hemangioma
rejected.why: While hemangiomas can be vascular, they do not typically present with the systemic findings or significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin levels seen in this case.
